goals.name: Email Sequence Session Harness
goals.description: Email Sequence Session Harness [email-sequence-session] — compiled from capabilities/harnesses/hB-13-email-sequence-session.yaml
goals.gate: Trigger, goal, ladder, and cadence all machine-validated.

gates.name: IG-01 Confirm the sequence trigger (lead magnet / trial / webinar
gates.description: Confirm the sequence trigger (lead magnet / trial / webinar / cold-warm) and its entry condition before writing email 1.

gates.name: IG-02 Confirm the conversion goal and the email-by-email escalatio
gates.description: Confirm the conversion goal and the email-by-email escalation ladder are declared up front.

gates.name: IG-03 Refuse fake-urgency mechanics (fake deadlines, fake 're:' su
gates.description: Refuse fake-urgency mechanics (fake deadlines, fake 're:' subjects) — session halts if requested.

gates.name: IG-04 Confirm suppression rules (customers, active opportunities)
gates.description: Confirm suppression rules (customers, active opportunities) are defined before any send logic.

gates.name: CG-01 Trigger & goal lock
gates.description: Entry trigger, exit conditions, and conversion goal locked in sequence.yaml.
gates.command: $SESS/sequence.yaml parses with keys trigger, exit_conditions[], goal; validator exits 0

gates.name: CG-02 Escalation ladder
gates.description: Email count 4-7; each email declares its ladder role (deliver, teach, story, proof, offer, urgency-honest, breakup); roles are non-repeating except proof.

gates.name: CG-03 Cadence justification
gates.description: Delay between emails documented with reason; no gap <1 day or >7 days without written justification.

gates.name: CG-04 Subject line bank
gates.description: >=2 subject candidates per email, <=60 chars, no fake 're:'/'fwd:' prefixes, no spam tokens.

gates.name: CG-05 Body format discipline
gates.description: Each email 75-200 words, one CTA, PS line optional and <=30 words.

gates.name: CG-06 Link integrity
gates.description: All links across all emails resolve and carry UTM tags with sequence name.

gates.name: CG-07 Suppression & exit wiring
gates.description: Suppression lists and goal-achieved early-exit are declared and mapped to ESP automation fields.
gates.command: $SESS/suppression.yaml parses with lists[] and early_exit_field; `python3 scripts/esp_map.py $SESS/suppression.yaml $SESS/esp_fields.json` exits 0

gates.name: CG-08 Compliance footer
gates.description: Unsubscribe link + sender address present in every email; plain-text twins exist for all.
gates.command: `grep -rL unsubscribe $SESS/emails/ | wc -l` == 0; `for f in $SESS/emails/*.md; do test -f ${f%.md}.txt || exit 1; done` exits 0

gates.name: CG-09 Personalization fallback
gates.description: Every merge tag has a declared fallback; rendering with empty contact data produces no raw {{...}} tokens.

gates.name: CG-10 Proof packet seal
gates.description: Sequence yaml, emails, subjects, suppression map hashed.

preconditions.startup_phrase: I am the Email Sequence operator. Every email earns the next open; every delay has a reason; every subscriber can leave in one click.

self_improvement.pattern_cadence: After every 5 sessions, mine the JSONL log for recurring gate failures, degrade waivers, and proof-command runtime outliers; write findings to ~/.rig/logs/harnesses/patterns/email-sequence-session-patterns.md.
self_improvement.update_trigger: If any single gate fails in >=30% of logged sessions over a rolling 20-session window, OR a new platform constraint (algorithm change, policy update, format deprecation) invalidates a proof command, propose a harness revision: bump the gate's proof, adjust its threshold, or split the gate — then re-seal with a new version hash.

success_conditions: Trigger, goal, ladder, and cadence all machine-validated.
Every email within format band with one CTA and clean link set.
Suppression and early-exit wiring mapped to ESP fields.
Compliance footer and plain-text twins present for 100% of emails.
Proof packet sealed; merge tags render clean on empty data.
failure_states: halt: Stop the session immediately. Record the failing gate id, the proof command output, and the missing prerequisite in $SESS/proof/halt_log.yaml. Do not draft past a halt gate; resume only after the gate's proof exits 0.

degrade: Continue the session with the deficit logged in $SESS/proof/waivers.md (gate id, reason, owner). A degrade-tier failure blocks 'clean ship' status — the Definition of Done must record the waiver explicitly.

stop: Terminal condition. Seal whatever proof exists, write $SESS/proof/stop_reason.md, and exit. No outward action (publish, send, deploy) may follow a stop-tier failure without human Gate-D approval.

final_rule: Ship only what the gates can prove. No artifact leaves this session on adjectives — every claim is bound to a command, a file, or a hash. A blocked gate is information, not failure; log it, learn from it, and make the next session's proof stronger. The operator who follows this harness leaves the system stronger than it found it.
